corpus_state_when_written.note: Counts are context, not criteria. A criterion that depends on a corpus count is a criterion that decays.

rules: A criterion is fixed at the moment it is written. If it turns out to be the wrong question, the run is recorded as a failure and a corrected measure is written beside it. The criterion is not moved.
Expected coverage was derived by reading the frameworks, not by running a search. Every MUST cell names a witness control that a person can open and check.

MUST means the framework demonstrably addresses the topic. NONE means it demonstrably does not, and a hit from it near the top is a precision failure. MAY is neither: present but incidental, so it neither earns credit nor costs any.
NONE is a strong claim and is used only where the absence was confirmed by reading. Where absence was merely not observed, the cell is MAY.

areas.name: Known-item retrieval
areas.measures: Whether the one control a person had in mind comes back at all.
areas.method: For every topic below, run the topic query. Check the witness control for each MUST framework.
areas.pass: Every named witness appears in the top 10 results for its topic. No exceptions.

areas.name: Identifier lookup
areas.measures: Whether typing a control's own identifier returns that control.
areas.method: Run each identifier case through exact lookup, not through topical search.
areas.pass: Each case resolves to exactly its expected control, or to exactly its expected ambiguity set. A topical score is never used to break a tie. Zero results for a well-formed identifier is a failure.

areas.name: Vocabulary equivalence
areas.measures: Whether two publishers writing the same requirement in different words reach each other.
areas.method: For each pair, run the left query and require the right control in the results.
areas.pass: Every pair connects. A pair that fails is reported with the term that was missing, not quietly widened.

areas.name: Cross-framework recall
areas.measures: Whether a topic query finds the topic everywhere it exists.
areas.method: For each topic, collect the distinct frameworks represented in the top 25.
areas.pass: Every MUST framework for that topic is represented. Missing one is a failure even if the result set looks good.

areas.name: Precision
areas.measures: Whether a topic query stays on topic.
areas.method: Inspect the top 5 for each topic.
areas.pass: No control from a NONE framework appears in the top 5, and at least 4 of the 5 are on the topic when read.

areas.name: Negative controls
areas.measures: Whether the tool says nothing when there is nothing.
areas.pass: Fewer than 3 results above the absolute score floor, and the tool states that it found nothing rather than presenting weak matches as answers.

areas.name: Abbreviations and collisions
areas.measures: Whether short forms resolve, and whether a short form that means two things is disambiguated.
areas.pass: Each abbreviation reaches its expansion. ISM as a query returns Information Security Manual controls; SP 800-88's use of ISM for information storage media never appears above them.

areas.name: Input robustness
areas.measures: Whether malformed input degrades or crashes.
areas.pass: No exception, no empty page without an explanation, and no result set that ignores the query entirely.

areas.name: Determinism
areas.measures: Whether the same question gets the same answer.
areas.method: Run every topic query twice in one process, then again after a full corpus rebuild.
areas.pass: Identical ordering and identical scores in all three runs, byte for byte.

areas.name: Ranking discipline
areas.measures: Whether the ordering carries the meaning it claims to.
areas.pass: Every ranking case holds. These are assertions about order, not about presence, and a case that passes only because one side is missing is a vacuous pass and counts as a failure.

multi-factor authentication.note: WA CSP is MAY, not MUST: it mandates the Essential Eight rather than naming multi-factor authentication.

media sanitisation and disposal.note: CSF 2.0 has no media sanitisation subcategory, and neither statute mentions it. This is the topic where an empty tier-1 and tier-3 band is the correct answer.

event logging and retention.note: CSF is MUST but says 'Log records are generated', never 'event log'. It is here to force the vocabulary to bridge that gap rather than to reward a literal match.

incident notification timeframes.query: how quickly must a cyber security incident be reported
incident notification timeframes.note: The Australian side states 12 hours (SOCI s 30BC), 72 hours (s 30BD), 4 hours to triage and 24 hours to report (WA CSP 5.1b, 5.1c). No American publication in this corpus states a counterpart. The comparison must show an empty American column and say so.

cryptographic keys and algorithms.query: approved cryptographic algorithms and key lengths

application control.note: 800-53 is MUST and never writes 'application control'; CM-7(5) is titled Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception. The WA CSP witness 3.1.1a does not contain the phrase either — it mandates the Essential Eight, of which application control is one strategy. Reaching it therefore requires expanding 'Essential Eight' into the eight strategy names ASD publishes. That is the hardest cell in this table and it is deliberate: a literal-text search cannot pass it.

supply chain and third parties.query: supply chain and third party risk

ranking.case: Query 'reporting a cyber security incident'. The SOCI Act notification provision must rank above any CIS benchmark configuration detail on the same subject.
ranking.why: A statutory obligation is the answer to that question; a product setting is not.

ranking.case: Query 'AC-6(5)'. The exact control must rank first, above any control whose text merely mentions privileged accounts.
ranking.why: Exact identifier lookup is a separate path and must win.

ranking.case: Query 'password policy'. A general control from the ISM or 800-53 must rank above any product-specific CIS benchmark setting.
ranking.why: Product baselines answer how to configure one product, not what is required.

ranking.case: Each ranking case must first assert that both sides of the comparison are present in the result set.
ranking.why: A ranking assertion that passes because the loser is missing has tested nothing.
